chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb al-Aḥmar, from ʿĀmir ibn Judhāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him say: The menstruating woman does not apply dye, nor does the junub; and she should not enter janabah while dye is upon her; and he should not enter janabah while dye is upon him; and he should not apply dye while he is junub.

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْخِضَابُ: dye applied to the body or hair
key_terms.تَخْتَضِبُ: she applies dye, such as henna
key_terms.تُجْنِبُ: she enters the state of janabah
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: he enters the state of janabah

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about using dye while in janabah or menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith states rulings concerning applying dye in relation to menstruation and janabah. It indicates disapproval or prohibition of dyeing while in the state of janabah or menstruation, and also of entering janabah while dye remains upon the body.
